design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (workflow task, difficulty savings_withdrawals_interest_and_transfers, M=2). Current as of round 8; the revision log at the end records how it got here.

[Scope snapshot] Claimed here: extended policies savings_ext_certificate_proceeds_transfer, savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation, savings_ext_best_money_market_conversion; the single workflow savings_wf_dormant_account_wakeup_and_upgrade; task tools transfer_savings_to_checking_5f60835b (user), reactivate_savings_account_bfe70db1, refund_savings_maintenance_fee_bf99bb2f, convert_savings_tier_d500151b. Task 1 claims the excess-withdrawal reconciliation space (certificate-funding fee refund, fee assessment, replenishment transfer) with its own three tools; nothing overlaps. The maintenance-fee refund step of the workflow carries no extended policy: it is decided under the base policies.

[Why this is a good test] Lorraine Hadley says only "I want to move my money market account up to the best money market account you have that I can get into." The conversion value (variant_name) comes from a downward search over the money market tiers that reads the account's status, its balance and whether the customer holds an active Private Client Checking account. The account is dormant (last customer-initiated activity 2024-08-12), and the conversion policy leaves a non-active account in its current tier, so the agent must first reactivate it; reactivation needs a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact, which here is the owner's telephone transfer of her certificate money to her checking account. The ledger also carries a 12.00 maintenance fee of cycle 2026-08 that base makes a bank error (the Money Market Account's minimum-daily-balance waiver of 2,500.00 was met: the lowest end-of-day balance of that cycle is 25,317.30), and the conversion reads the balance after every refund owed has posted. After the transfer the balance is 24,993.99; with the refund it is 25,005.99, just over the 25,000.00 Private Client Money Market minimum. An agent that skips reactivation gets no conversion; an agent that skips the refund gets Premier Money Market; an agent that misreads the certificate money moves the wrong amount.

[Problem-tree card] root_problem = savings_ext_best_money_market_conversion (step 13). Edge 1: root -> savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation, value_input, gate = compute binding active; condition "A dormant account has been reactivated through a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact before any conversion is recorded."; policy_source "The account must be active when the conversion is recorded, so a dormant account is converted only after the owner has made a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact and the account has been reactivated."; resolved_by reactivate_savings_account_bfe70db1; false at frozen_time because initial_state.savings_accounts.<mma>.status = dormant. Edge 2: savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation -> savings_ext_certificate_proceeds_transfer, value_input, gate = compute binding d; condition "The transfer the owner makes in the contact has posted before the reactivation date is recorded."; policy_source (reactivation rule) "The transfer made in the contact is the latest withdrawal on the account with channel telephone_banking, online_transfer or mobile_app_transfer, so the reactivation date is the latest posted_date among the account's withdrawals with those three channels"; resolved_by transfer_savings_to_checking_5f60835b; false because no transfer has been made in this contact: the latest such withdrawal on the ledger is the online transfer of 2024-08-12. Shape: a chain conversion -> reactivation -> transfer. Topological order: transfer (7), reactivation (9), conversion (13); the base refund (11) sits between reactivation and conversion and commutes with the reactivation. Deletion sensitivity (check_compute value_input replay and hand replay): without step 9 the account stays dormant and the conversion computes the current tier 'Money Market Account'; without step 7 the reactivation compute reads the 2024-08-12 online transfer instead of a transfer of this contact (d = 2024-08-12 instead of 2026-09-11), and no reactivation under this policy applies. The customer names none of these problems, and no tool validates anything.

[Base-invariant card] Step 7 (savings_withdrawal): savings_evt_withdrawal_allowance.status_allows_withdrawal ("Withdrawals are paid only from an account whose status is active or dormant.") holds, status dormant; covered_by_balance holds, 10,411.98 <= 35,405.97; savings_evt_closure has no gate for savings_withdrawal (scope only, not a closure payout). Telephone_banking is a counted channel of the Money Market Account but it is the first counted withdrawal of cycle 2026-10 (free 6), so no excess fee arises. Step 9 (savings_reactivate): savings_evt_dormancy.verified_owner satisfied by the step 1 verification_log row. Step 11 (savings_fee_refund, base-governed): eligible_fee_code (monthly_maintenance), courtesy_window (anchor savings_transactions.posted_date 2026-08-10, 60 calendar days from the next day, inclusive, last allowed day 2026-10-09; frozen 2026-09-11 is day 32; the gate's own arithmetic, a bank_error refund having no time limit), courtesy_limit (none used, limit 2), account_open (dormant before step 9, active after, both allowed), refund_once (no refund points at the fee); the bank-error ground is base's: savings_evt_maintenance_and_statement_fees makes the minimum-daily-balance waiver met for 2026-08 (lowest end-of-day balance 25,317.30 against 2,500.00), and savings_evt_fee_refund refunds such a fee in full as bank_error. Step 13 (savings_change_product): must_be_active satisfied by the step 9 state effect; target entry gate for Private Client Money Market: an active Private Client Checking account (ending 3082, active since 2015) and balance >= 25,000.00 (25,005.99); per-tier cap 2, none held; age 68 >= 18.

[Business-object card] Target account: Money Market Account ending 2459 (the only savings account). Certificate money = rows with counterparty_account_id = the 12-Month Certificate ending 2893, which made the most recent internal-transfer deposit (the 2026-08-25 maturity payout) and whose payout_account_id is this account: 13 interest payouts 2025-08-31..2026-08-14 (411.98) + maturity payout (10,000.00) = 10,411.98; excluded: the account's own interest credits, the 2023-2024 customer deposits and withdrawals, fees. Reactivating transaction: the one withdrawal posted on 2026-09-11, to checking 3082. Fee refunded: the single monthly_maintenance row (12.00, cycle 2026-08, posted 2026-08-10); the dormant_account fee 5.00 of 2026-09 is correct and is not refunded; the customer declines goodwill waivers.

[World rows] customers (identity; four verification credentials); checking_accounts Private Client Checking (transfer destination, the reactivation policy's own-checking check, the Private Client Money Market entry gate); cd_certificates 12-Month Certificate closed 2026-08-25 (identifies certificate money; its payouts are internal transfers, not customer-initiated, which is why the account still went dormant); savings_accounts row dormant; 99 ledger rows: opening, check and mobile deposits and two online transfers up to 2024-08-12 (last customer activity), 39 cycles of base and relationship-bonus interest credits computed day by day on the tiered ladder with the 0.15 bonus, the certificate payouts, the erroneous maintenance fee and the dormant fee. current_balance 35,405.97 equals the ledger sum. Automatic clauses checked: no maintenance fee in the dormant cycle 2026-09, interest continues while dormant, no automatic transfer, promo never qualified, so nothing else is owed.

[Persona design] Lorraine Hadley, 68, retired librarian, brisk and organised; she opens with the surface goal in her own words and wants this account moved, not a new one. Given only when asked: mobile 3365550133, date of birth 1958-04-17, SSN last four 2716, ZIP 27408, email only if verification still fails, account ending 2459, checking ending 3082. Passive reactions: only after the agent says a transaction of hers is needed today does she say "Then move the money my certificate paid into it over to my checking", without knowing the figure; she runs the handed-over transfer tool with the details the agent gives; she refuses goodwill favours; she closes when told the new tier and asks for one re-check if told it cannot move. She never mentions fees, dormancy or refunds.

[Zero-wait causal card, workflow steps] Step 0 transfer (action 7): needs the account and balance, the certificate rows and the destination checking (initial_state_preexisting) and her instruction (current_user_input); effect: a posted withdrawal whose posted_date is the business day it posts, 2026-09-11, because the frozen date is a Friday and no Federal Reserve holiday (the tool applies the base convention "Business day the withdrawal posted" mechanically: on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal Reserve holiday it would post on the next business day, after the contact, the reactivation policy would establish no date, and the workflow, which applies to a contact on a business day, would not run). Step 1 reactivation (9): needs the verified owner (prior_synchronous_tool_effect of verify_customer_identity at 1) and the transfer she makes in this contact to her own checking (prior_synchronous_tool_effect of step 7, the only telephone, online or mobile withdrawal posted on 2026-09-11; posted_date feeds reactivation_date through dataflow object_binding); effect: status active. Step 2 refund (11, base-governed): needs the fee row and the cycle's ledger (initial_state_preexisting); effect: +12.00 credit posted 2026-09-11 (the refund tool follows the same business-day posting convention). Step 3 conversion (13): needs status active (prior_synchronous_tool_effect of step 9, dataflow state_effect establishing savings_product_change.must_be_active) and the balance after steps 7 and 11, both posted on 2026-09-11 so that no row on the account has a posted_date after the frozen date; effect: variant_name changed. Nothing waits for clearing, review, a batch or a future date.

[Policy -> workflow -> GT closure] savings_ext_certificate_proceeds_transfer -> step 0 transfer tool (subject savings_withdrawal) -> computation step 7 amount 10411.98. savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation -> step 1 reactivation tool (subject savings_reactivate, base refs savings_evt_dormancy) -> computation step 9 reactivation_date 2026-09-11. Step 2 refund tool (subject savings_fee_refund, base refs savings_evt_fee_refund) computed_by [] -> base-governed 12.00 bank_error. savings_ext_best_money_market_conversion -> step 3 conversion tool (subject savings_change_product) -> computation step 13 variant_name Private Client Money Market. set(workflow computed_by) = set(computations.policy_id) = charter_scope.extended_policies = required_documents (same order).

[Rule <-> compute sweep] Transfer: the certificate that most recently paid in -> d_in (latest internal-transfer deposit date), cd_cp (its counterparty), same_cp (every internal-transfer deposit of that date has that counterparty, so no row order is used) and cd_id (exact certificate id, also requiring payout_account_id = this account); deposits from it -> cd_in; withdrawals back to it with zero floor -> cd_back, net_cd; cap at balance and rounding -> bal, result (cap untriggered). Reactivation: "An account that is not dormant is not reactivated" -> is_dormant; the latest posted_date among telephone, online and mobile withdrawals -> d_tel, d_onl, d_mob (mobile untriggered), d (the date is the same whichever of several same-day rows is read, so no row order is used); "exactly one withdrawal with those three channels posted on that date" -> n_on_d; its counterparty -> cp; "a checking account of the same customer" -> own (exact-id CFIELD read); "the date is established under this policy only when that posted date is not after the frozen date, the day of the contact" -> not_after_contact (d <= NOW); result = d or ''. The transfer tool writes the business day as posted_date, so on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal Reserve holiday d is the next business day, after the frozen date, and the compute, the rule and base savings_withdrawal.posted_date all give no reactivation date under this policy; on a business day d is the frozen date. That the transfer was made in this contact is a condition the rule states is established from the contact itself and not tested by the computed date, like the conversion's cap. Conversion: downward search and stop at the current tier -> result; "An account that is not active when the target is chosen stays in its current tier" -> active; Private Client gate -> pc_chk, pc_ok, pcmm_ok; Premier and Money Market minimums -> premier_ok, mma_ok; top tier stays -> already_top (untriggered); balance after the owner's transfer and every refund owed -> bal. The per-tier cap and the other entry gates are eligibility checked after the target is chosen, as the rule states, not compute bindings. The rule's condition that no transaction on the account has a posted_date later than the frozen date is likewise a record-read applicability condition that the computed target does not test; here the latest posted_date is 2026-09-11. Every compute_basis quotation is a verbatim substring of its rule (checked mechanically).

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify (phone, DOB, SSN4, ZIP) -> find_savings_accounts -> find_savings_transactions (whole ledger) -> find_checking_accounts -> find_cd_certificates -> explain that a transaction of hers is needed -> hand over the transfer tool; she transfers 10,411.98 to checking 3082 with statement_cycle 2026-10 -> reactivate with date 2026-09-11 -> refund the 12.00 fee as bank_error under the base waivers, statement_cycle 2026-10 -> convert to Private Client Money Market.

[Verification] check_compute --task 0 replays gold with the real tools and recomputes each policy at handling time: transfer 10411.98 (before step 7), reactivation 2026-09-11 (before step 9), conversion 'Private Client Money Market' (before step 13, balance 25,005.99, active); value_input replay without step 9 gives 'Money Market Account'; forcing cross-category reads off changes all three results; zeroing history changes the transfer and the reactivation. Gates (round 5): EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (closure 103/103), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[solvability_contract vs GT] Each of the 4 calls lists every gate of every base policy governing its subject; bindings resolve to the same account, fee and customer ids that gold passes; the step 13 must_be_active evidence is prior_step:9 per the workflow state_effect; the step 9 verified_owner evidence is prior_step:1; the courtesy_window entry at step 11 deep-copies the base temporal_basis with boundary days 2026-10-09 / 2026-10-10.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Using only the published rules, the tool schemas, the lookups and her lines: the conversion rule says a non-active account stays in its tier and that a dormant account is converted only after reactivation through a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact -> the reactivation rule takes the posted date of the transfer she makes in this contact to her own checking, the latest such withdrawal and the only one that day -> she asks for the certificate money: sum of deposits from certificate 2893 = 10,411.98 -> reactivation dated 2026-09-11. The conversion reads the balance after every refund owed: the base waiver rules show the 2026-08 maintenance fee was charged although the minimum-daily-balance waiver was met (lowest end-of-day balance 25,317.30) -> bank_error refund 12.00. Balance 35,405.97 - 10,411.98 + 12.00 = 25,005.99 >= 25,000 with Private Client Checking -> Private Client Money Market. Same objects, order and values as gold.

[Most likely mistakes] converting a dormant account; refunding as courtesy_waiver; forgetting the refund and landing on Premier; summing only the maturity payout or adding the account's own interest; using the fee's cycle 2026-08 as the refund's statement_cycle; dating reactivation 2024-08-12.

[Revision log] Round 1: first draft. Round 2: overwrites were declared for the linked-checking maintenance-fee refund; the Private Client Checking test became existential. Round 3: first-row lookups removed (certificate by exact counterparty; per-tier status test); the conversion's cap stated as eligibility; the automatic-transfer waiver left to base. Round 4: the overwrites were withdrawn and the linked-checking refund was tied to record-position conditions. Round 5 (policy_task revision_4 R4-1): those conditions could not be established from any record, so savings_ext_linked_waiver_maintenance_refund was withdrawn; the maintenance-fee refund is now a base-governed workflow step (computed_by []) resting on the ledger-verifiable minimum-daily-balance waiver, and the problem tree now runs conversion <- savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation (value_input through the conversion's new active binding) <- transfer (state_gate), with the reactivation date computed from the posted date of the transfer to the owner's own checking. A reseed experiment (online transfer of 2024-08-12 at 425.00) was tried and reverted; the world, the transfer (10,411.98), the refund (12.00) and the target (Private Client Money Market) are unchanged.


[Revision log, round 6 (audit rework)] Symptoms (policy_task revision_5 R5-1): the round-5 reactivation policy identified the transaction made in the contact by the frozen date alone (a pre-call transfer that morning would qualify, and on a non-business day the transfer posts on the next business day), and its per-channel most-recent lookup within a day depended on row order. Change: the reactivation date is now the latest posted_date among the account's telephone, online and mobile withdrawals, which is the same whichever of several same-day rows is read; it is established only when exactly one such withdrawal posted that date and its counterparty is one of the customer's checking accounts, so no row order is ever used; the date follows the withdrawal's business-day posted_date instead of the frozen date; and that the transfer was made in this contact is stated as a condition established from the contact itself, not by the computed date. The same-day tie was also removed from the certificate lookup of the proceeds transfer (all internal-transfer deposits on the latest date must share one counterparty). Edge 2 is now declared value_input with gate d (R5-O1). Values unchanged: transfer 10,411.98, reactivation 2026-09-11, refund 12.00, Private Client Money Market.


[Revision log, round 7 (audit rework)] Symptom (policy_task revision_6 R6-1): the transfer tool dated its withdrawal today on any day, while the base field savings_withdrawal.posted_date says "Business day the withdrawal posted" and the reactivation rule relies on that, so a Saturday contact gave 2026-09-12 by compute and 2026-09-14 by rule and base. Change: the transfer tool now posts the withdrawal on the business day it posts (today when today is Monday through Friday and not a Federal Reserve holiday, otherwise the next business day), its docstring and receipt say so, and its statement_cycle argument is the cycle containing that posted date; the reactivation rule now says a transfer made on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal Reserve holiday posts on the next business day and that posted date is the reactivation date. The compute is unchanged and now agrees with rule and base on every day (a Saturday 2026-09-12 contact gives 2026-09-14 in all three). This world is a Friday, so the transfer still posts 2026-09-11; the argument proofs of the transfer's statement_cycle and of the reactivation date now cite the business-day fact. Values unchanged: transfer 10,411.98, reactivation 2026-09-11, refund 12.00, Private Client Money Market.


[Revision log, round 8 (audit rework)] Symptoms (policy_task revision_7 R7-1, R7-O1): the two refund tools and the fee tool still dated their rows today with the account's current statement cycle, against the base fields "Business day the refund posted" and "Business day the fee posted" (the maintenance refund of this workflow is one of them); and on a non-business-day contact the owner's transfer posts only on the next business day, so reactivating and converting in that contact would rest on a transfer that has not posted. Changes: every posting tool now posts on the business day it posts (today on a business day, otherwise the next business day), with statement_cycle the cycle that contains that posted date for the refunds, and returns the posted_date; the reactivation date is established only when the transfer's posted date is not after the frozen date, the day of the contact (compute binding not_after_contact), which replaces the round-7 sentence that made a weekend transfer's posted date the reactivation date; the conversion applies only when no row on the account has a posted_date later than the frozen date; the workflow now applies to a contact on a business day. This world is a Friday: the transfer and the refund post 2026-09-11, not_after_contact is true and no row is later than 2026-09-11. Values unchanged: transfer 10,411.98, reactivation 2026-09-11, refund 12.00 with statement_cycle 2026-10, Private Client Money Market.
user_scenario:
You are Lorraine Hadley, a 68-year-old retired school librarian in Greensboro who likes to get to the point and keeps her papers in a folder by the phone. You are calling Piedmont Crescent Bank and you open with it in your own words: "I want to move my money market account up to the best money market account you have that I can get into." You say that plainly at the start, and you add that you have heard the bank has fancier money market tiers and you want the highest one they will let you have; you do not want to open a new account, you want this one moved over.

You give your details only as the agent asks for them. Your mobile number is 3365550133. If asked for verification, you give your date of birth as 1958-04-17, the last four of your Social Security number as 2716 and your ZIP code as 27408; you would rather not recite your email, and you only give it (lorraine.hadley58@gmail.com) if the agent says it still cannot verify you. The account you mean is your money market account ending in 2459; you also have a Private Client checking account ending in 3082, and you mention the checking account only when the agent asks about it or asks where money should go. You do not know your balances or rates by heart and tell the agent to look them up.

Once the agent tells you that you have to make a transaction of your own on the money market account today before anything can be changed, you say that suits you fine: "Then move the money my certificate paid into it over to my checking." You mean everything your old 12-month certificate put into that account, its interest and the money it paid out when it matured, and all of it should go to your checking ending in 3082. You do not know the exact figure and ask the agent to add it up from the records. When the agent hands you a tool to make that transfer yourself, you use it with the account details and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation it shows you if the agent asks.

If the agent offers to waive or refund some other small charge as a favor, you tell them you do not want favors, only whatever the bank actually owes you under its own rules. You do not ask about fees, interest or the account's status, and you do not suggest any step yourself. When the agent tells you which tier the account has been moved to, you thank them, say that is exactly what you wanted, and end the call. If the agent says the account can only stay where it is, you ask them to double-check once against the records; if they confirm it again, you accept that and end the call.

base_preconditions.condition: Withdrawals are paid only from an account whose status is active or dormant.

A withdrawal is paid only when its amount does not exceed the current balance; a withdrawal that would take the balance below zero is declined and never posts, except an overdraft protection transfer, which the checking charter makes only when the savings balance covers it in full.
Closure governs a payout withdrawal only when the account is being closed; this transfer is not a closure payout, so savings_evt_closure applies only as scope.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.savings_account_id: Id 195afab4-5633-473d-b719-2ed2be3f89e0: the money market account ending 2459 that the customer names ("your money market account ending in 2459"), returned by find_savings_accounts; it is her only savings account, so no other id fits.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.destination_checking_account_id: Id of the Private Client Checking account ending 3082 returned by find_checking_accounts; the customer says the money "should go to your checking ending in 3082" and it is her only checking account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 10411.98, computed by savings_ext_certificate_proceeds_transfer: the most recent internal-transfer deposit is the 10,000.00 maturity payout of 2026-08-25 from the 12-Month Certificate ending 2893, a certificate of the customer whose payout account is this account; deposits from it = 13 interest payouts totalling 411.98 + 10,000.00 = 10,411.98; withdrawals sent to it = 0.00; cap at the balance 35,405.97 does not bind; rounded to the cent = 10,411.98.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.statement_cycle: 2026-10. Basis: the docstring defines it as "the YYYY-MM month in which the statement cycle that contains the withdrawal's posted date closes" and gives the posted date as "today when today is a business day (Monday through Friday, other than a Federal Reserve holiday)"; the frozen date 2026-09-11 is a Friday and no Federal Reserve holiday, so the transfer posts 2026-09-11; the account's statement_cycle_day is 10, so 2026-09-11 falls after the 2026-09-10 close and its cycle closes 2026-10-10. 2026-09 is the cycle already closed and any later month does not contain the posted date, so 2026-10 is unique.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock reactivate_savings_account_bfe70db1 so it can be called (reactivation of the dormant account).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect; each tool is unlocked once in this task.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Return the dormant account to active status with 2026-09-11, the date of the owner's transfer, as its latest customer-initiated activity.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation computes reactivation_date; savings_product_change requires the account to be active when a conversion is recorded.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.savings_account_id: Id 195afab4-5633-473d-b719-2ed2be3f89e0: the same dormant money market account, from find_savings_accounts; it is the only dormant account of the customer.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Id of Lorraine Hadley's profile, returned by find_customers and verified at step 1; the docstring asks for the owner whose identity was verified in this conversation.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reactivation_date: 2026-09-11, computed by savings_ext_same_contact_reactivation: the account is dormant; the owner's telephone transfer made in this contact (step 7) is the latest telephone, online or mobile withdrawal on the account, posted 2026-09-11 (a Friday and so a business day, on which the transfer posts the day it is made), so that posted date is not after the frozen date, the day of the contact; it is the only such withdrawal that day and its counterparty is her Private Client Checking ending 3082, a checking account of the same customer; so the reactivation date is that posted date. No other customer-initiated transaction exists in this contact.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock refund_savings_maintenance_fee_bf99bb2f so it can be called (bank-error refund of the maintenance fee).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect; each tool is unlocked once in this task.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Refund the 12.00 maintenance fee of cycle 2026-08 as a bank error, because base waivers were met for that cycle.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Base savings_evt_fee_refund: a maintenance fee in a cycle where a waiver was met is a bank_error refund in full. The Money Market Account's minimum-daily-balance waiver (2,500.00) was met: the lowest end-of-day balance over 2026-07-11..2026-08-10 on the ledger is 25,317.30. The conversion rule reads the balance after every refund owed has posted, so the refund precedes the conversion.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.savings_account_id: Id 195afab4-5633-473d-b719-2ed2be3f89e0: the account that carries the fee, from find_savings_accounts.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: Id of the owner's profile from find_customers; it equals the customer_id on the fee row.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_item_id: Id of the 12.00 monthly_maintenance fee row of cycle 2026-08 posted 2026-08-10, from find_savings_transactions; it is the only maintenance fee on the account.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 12.00. Basis: savings_evt_fee_refund "A fee is refunded in full, never in part" and "A bank_error refund applies when the fee was assessed contrary to the savings charter, such as ... a maintenance fee in a cycle where a waiver was met"; savings_evt_maintenance_and_statement_fees lists the waiver "savings_msr_cycle_min_daily_balance at or above waiver_min_daily_balance" (Money Market Account 2,500.00), and the ledger gives a lowest end-of-day balance of 25,317.30 for cycle 2026-08. The fee's posted amount is 12.00, so the refund is 12.00; no partial amount is allowed.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.adjustment_reason: bank_error. Basis: savings_evt_fee_refund: "A bank_error refund applies when the fee was assessed contrary to the savings charter, such as ... a maintenance fee in a cycle where a waiver was met". courtesy_waiver is for a correctly assessed fee and would consume the courtesy limit; none is not a refund ground.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.statement_cycle: 2026-10. Basis: savings_fee_refund "statement_cycle: Statement cycle in which the refund posted" and the docstring's "the YYYY-MM month in which the statement cycle that contains the refund's posted date closes", with the posted date "today when today is a business day (Monday through Friday, other than a Federal Reserve holiday)"; 2026-09-11 is a Friday and no Federal Reserve holiday, so the refund posts 2026-09-11, after the 2026-09-10 close, and its cycle closes 2026-10-10. Using the fee's own cycle 2026-08 would contradict the field meaning.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock convert_savings_tier_d500151b so it can be called (tier conversion).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect; each tool is unlocked once in this task.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Convert the account to Private Client Money Market, the highest money market tier it qualifies for once it is active and its balance reflects the owner's transfer and the refund.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: savings_ext_best_money_market_conversion computes variant_name on the reactivated account, on the balance after the owner's transfer and the refund owed.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.savings_account_id: Id 195afab4-5633-473d-b719-2ed2be3f89e0: the account the customer asks to move up, from find_savings_accounts.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.variant_name: Private Client Money Market, computed by savings_ext_best_money_market_conversion: the account is active after the step 9 reactivation; at handling time the balance is 25,005.99 (35,405.97 - 10,411.98 owner's transfer + 12.00 refund); the customer holds an active Private Client Checking account and 25,005.99 >= 25,000.00, so the top-ranked money market tier qualifies first. Premier Money Market and Money Market Account rank lower; staying in the current tier applies only when the account is not active or no higher tier qualifies.

edges.condition: A dormant account has been reactivated through a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact before any conversion is recorded.
edges.policy_source: The account must be active when the conversion is recorded, so a dormant account is converted only after the owner has made a customer-initiated transaction in the same contact and the account has been reactivated.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time the account is dormant: its latest customer-initiated activity is 2024-08-12, more than 24 months earlier, so it is not active and the must_be_active gate of savings_product_change is false.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The step 9 reactivation sets savings_accounts.status to active with last_customer_activity_date 2026-09-11, so active becomes true.

edges.condition: The transfer the owner makes in the contact has posted before the reactivation date is recorded.
edges.policy_source: The transfer made in the contact is the latest withdrawal on the account with channel telephone_banking, online_transfer or mobile_app_transfer, so the reactivation date is the latest posted_date among the account's withdrawals with those three channels

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen_time no transfer has been made in this contact: the latest telephone, online or mobile withdrawal on the ledger is the online transfer of 2024-08-12, so d would be 2024-08-12, not a transfer of this contact, and no reactivation date for this contact exists.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The step 7 telephone transfer posts a 10,411.98 withdrawal dated 2026-09-11 to the owner's checking account ending 3082; d becomes 2026-09-11, n_on_d 1 and own true.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The order is fixed by the policies: the reactivation date is the posted date of the transfer made in the contact, so the transfer comes first; the conversion leaves a non-active account in its current tier, so the reactivation precedes it. The base-governed refund step (workflow step 2) adds 12.00 to the balance whether it posts before or after the reactivation, and the single workflow fixes it third.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replaying gold without the step 9 reactivation leaves status dormant at step 13, so active is false and the computed variant_name changes from 'Private Client Money Market' to the current tier 'Money Market Account' (verified by check_compute value_input replay); the terminal state also keeps last_customer_activity_date 2024-08-12.

Without the step 7 transfer the latest telephone, online or mobile withdrawal is the online transfer of 2024-08-12, so the reactivation policy would compute 2024-08-12 instead of 2026-09-11 (and, the transfer not being one made in this contact, no reactivation under this policy applies at all); the terminal state lacks the 10,411.98 transfer and the balance ends 35,417.97.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to move the old money market account up to the best money market tier she can get. It never mentions reactivation, inactivity, a transaction being needed, fees or refunds; her wish to move the certificate money is a passive reaction given only after the agent says a transaction of hers is needed today, and she never names any policy.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: convert_savings_tier_d500151b only updates variant_name; it reads no status, balance or checking data and would convert a dormant or under-funded account without error. reactivate_savings_account_bfe70db1 sets the status and date it is given without checking any transaction, and transfer_savings_to_checking_5f60835b posts any amount; none of the task tools checks a prerequisite, refuses or hints.

factor_trace: d_in = LATEST posted_date of internal_transfer deposits = 2026-08-25; cd_cp = counterparty of the internal-transfer deposit of that date = the 12-Month Certificate ending 2893 (its 10,000.00 maturity payout); same_cp = True (the only internal-transfer deposit that day); cd_id = CFIELD('cd','certificate_id', certificate_id=cd_cp, payout_account_id=HID) = that certificate (closed 2026-08-25, payout_account_id = this money market account) [history + cross-category read].

cd_in = SUM of savings_deposit rows with channel internal_transfer and counterparty that certificate = 13 monthly/final interest payouts 2025-08-31..2026-08-14 totalling 411.98 plus the 10,000.00 maturity payout = 10,411.98 [history].
cd_back = SUM of withdrawals on this account whose counterparty is that certificate = 0.00 (both withdrawals on the ledger went to checking 3082) [history].
bal = F('current_balance') at handling time = 35,405.97 [holding field].
result = RND(bal) if net_cd > bal else RND(net_cd): 10,411.98 > 35,405.97 is false, so the cap branch is untriggered and result = 10,411.98.
is_dormant = F('status') == 'dormant' = True (last customer-initiated activity 2024-08-12) [holding field].

d_tel = latest telephone_banking withdrawal date = 2026-09-11 (the owner's transfer at step 7, posted the same day because 2026-09-11 is a Friday business day); d_onl = 2024-08-12 (latest online transfer); d_mob = '' (no mobile transfer ever: untriggered branch) [history at handling time].
d = MX(2026-09-11, 2024-08-12, '') = 2026-09-11, the posted date of the transfer made in this contact.

not_after_contact = d <= NOW = 2026-09-11 <= 2026-09-11 = True: the transfer posted on the day of the contact, a business day (on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal Reserve holiday it would post on the next business day and this factor would be False).
n_on_d = 1 (one telephone, no online or mobile withdrawal posted on 2026-09-11) [history].
cp = counterparty of that withdrawal = checking account ending 3082; own = CFIELD('checking','checking_account_id', checking_account_id=cp) != None = True [cross-category read, exact id].

result = d = 2026-09-11 because the account is dormant, the date is not after the day of the contact, and exactly one such withdrawal, to the owner's own checking, posted on that date. That the transfer was made in this contact is established from the contact (the step 7 call), as the rule states.
bal = F('current_balance') at handling time = 35,405.97 - 10,411.98 (step 7 transfer) + 12.00 (step 11 refund) = 25,005.99 [holding field after prior gold writes].
cur = F('variant_name') = Money Market Account; already_top = False (untriggered branch).
active = F('status') == 'active' = True after the step 9 reactivation [holding field after prior gold writes].
pc_chk = CFIELD('checking','checking_account_id', variant_name='Private Client Checking', status='active') = the checking account ending 3082; pc_ok = True [cross-category read].

result = 'Private Client Money Market'. Without the step 9 reactivation the account is still dormant and the result would be the current tier 'Money Market Account'; without the base refund the balance would be 24,993.99 and the result 'Premier Money Market'; without Private Client Checking it would also be 'Premier Money Market'. The rule's applicability condition that no row on the account has a posted_date later than the frozen date holds: the latest posted_date after steps 7 and 11 is 2026-09-11.
